headline: ChatGPT Voice Mode now listens and speaks simultaneously
summary: OpenAI's GPT-Live model enables full-duplex conversations, allowing for more natural and uninterrupted interactions.
details: OpenAI has introduced GPT-Live, a new voice model for ChatGPT that offers a significant upgrade in conversational naturalness. Unlike previous versions that processed speech and text in separate steps, GPT-Live uses a full-duplex architecture, enabling it to listen and speak at the same time.

This advancement means ChatGPT can now provide real-time acknowledgements, like "mhmm" or "yeah," while you're speaking, mimicking human conversational flow. It also allows for more complex tasks to be passed to other models, such as GPT-5.5, for deeper reasoning or research.

The GPT-Live voice model is accessible via the ChatGPT app on Android and iOS, as well as through web browsers. Paid subscribers (Plus, Pro, and Go) get access to the GPT-Live-1 model, while free users can utilize the GPT-Live-1 mini model.

Users can initiate voice conversations by tapping the waveform symbol in the ChatGPT app. The interface now features a responsive floating orb, and users can adjust the intelligence level of the voice model to 'Instant,' 'Medium,' or 'High' for tailored response times, though this feature is exclusive to paid plans.

While GPT-Live enhances conversational fluidity, it currently does not support screen or video sharing. Users can, however, revert to the older voice model or customize voice options and language settings within the app's preferences.

headline_marked: Galaxy Z Fold 8 [[revives side fingerprint scanner]] — a decade-old feature
headline: Galaxy Z Fold 8 revives side fingerprint scanner — a decade-old feature
summary: The $1,900 Galaxy Z Fold 8 uses a side-mounted fingerprint scanner, a feature common on $100 phones from ten years ago, proving its convenience and reliability.
details: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, despite its premium $1,900 price tag, features a side-mounted fingerprint scanner integrated into the power button. This design choice, reminiscent of budget phones from a decade ago, has proven to be highly reliable and convenient for the reviewer.

This sensor works seamlessly whether the phone is folded or unfolded, always remaining in the same accessible position on the right edge. Its reliability has been noted over several weeks of use, with only a few instances requiring a second attempt to unlock the device.

While under-display fingerprint scanners are now standard on most flagship smartphones, they often present challenges. These can include struggling with wet or dirty fingers and requiring the screen to be on, unlike side-mounted sensors which can be activated by simply picking up the phone.

The reviewer highlights that side-mounted scanners are more convenient for many users, including themselves, as they allow for immediate unlocking upon raising the device. This contrasts with under-display sensors, which can be harder to tap accurately or require a separate button press.

Although side-mounted scanners are not as common in the current market, the Galaxy Z Fold 8's implementation suggests a potential resurgence. The reviewer expresses a desire to see this practical and user-friendly feature make a comeback in future smartphone designs.
